text: Before a salaried borrower gets a loan, someone checks their income by hand. Payslips, a bank statement, Form 16. It takes hours per file, and edited documents still slip through.
IncomeVerify does it in about two minutes. An AI model only reads the documents. Every check and every decision is plain code.
This is the queue. Each application shows its verdict, the verified income, and how authentic the documents look.
Let's run a sample with something planted in it. The latest payslip was edited. Every page is read, then each document is checked on its own.
A couple of minutes later, it's flagged. Six separate signs. The payslip maths doesn't add up, the PDF was saved by an editing tool, and that salary never reached the bank.
Every finding links to its source. Here is the edited net pay, boxed on the original payslip, in a font used nowhere else on the page.
Bank statements are checked row by row. An edited balance breaks the running total, and the row is shown right on the statement.
A reviewer can correct anything that was misread. Every change is logged, and the whole file is checked again.
Under the hood, OCR and an AI model only read. Everything in this box is plain Python. The model never calculates.
And it's measured. On thirty fresh test applicants, every planted fraud was caught, no honest file was flagged, and each one cost about five cents.
IncomeVerify, built by Sarthak Aggarwal. The code, the evals and the load tests are all on GitHub.
